text: By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat down and wept when we remembered Zion.
There, on the willow trees, we hung up our harps.
For there, our captors demanded songs from us, and our tormentors asked for joy, saying, sing us one of the songs of Zion.
How can we sing the LORD's song in a foreign land?
If I forget you, Jerusalem, may my right hand forget its skill.
May my tongue stick to the roof of my mouth if I do not remember you, if I do not consider Jerusalem my highest joy.
Remember, LORD, what the Edomites did on the day Jerusalem fell, how they said, tear it down, tear it down, all the way to its foundations.
Daughter Babylon, doomed to destruction, happy is the one who repays you for what you have done to us.
Happy is the one who seizes your infants and dashes them against the rocks.
